places: Hyatt Regency Hotel, Kansas City, Missouri

timeline.event: The Hartford Civic Center roof collapsed.
Construction began on the fast-tracked 40-story Hyatt Regency Kansas City.
A section of 2,700 square feet of the hotel's roof partially collapsed.
Engineer Daniel M. Duncan accepted Havens Steel's proposed design change via a phone call without performing necessary calculations or reviewing sketches.
Onsite workers noticed beams bending but neglected to report it, rerouting their heavy wheelbarrows around the unsteady walkways.
The Hyatt Regency Kansas City officially opened.
The fourth-floor walkway dropped several inches, paused, fell onto the second-floor walkway, and both crashed onto the crowded lobby floor during a tea dance.
timeline.place: Hyatt Regency Hotel, Kansas City, Missouri

timeline.event: Emergency medical director Joseph Waeckerle directed a 14-hour rescue operation with volunteers, construction suppliers, and first responders.
timeline.place: Hyatt Regency Hotel, Kansas City, Missouri

timeline.event: Final rescued victim Mark Williams was freed after spending more than nine hours pinned beneath the lower skywalk.
timeline.place: Hyatt Regency Hotel lobby, Kansas City, Missouri

timeline.event: Architectural engineer Wayne G. Lischka was hired by The Kansas City Star and discovered the critical change to the walkways' original design.
A laboratory at Lehigh University began testing box beams on behalf of the steel fabrication source.
The Hyatt Regency reopened after its atrium was redesigned and an engineering committee confirmed no other safety issues remained.

National Bureau of Standards lead investigator Edward Pfrang determined that the revised walkways possessed minimal capacity to resist their own weight and would fail under one-third of the weight held that night.
The Kansas City Star and the Kansas City Times were awarded a Pulitzer Prize for their 16 months of investigative coverage of the collapse.
Local authorities reported that a $5 million hotel reconstruction made the building possibly the safest in the country.
The Hyatt Regency disaster was cited in arguments against the Reagan administration's attempt to eliminate an agency of the National Bureau of Standards.
The hotel was renamed the Hyatt Regency Crown Center.

legacy.what: The hotel's atrium was redesigned, permanently removing the upper walkways, replacing the second-floor walkway with one supported by columns, and reinforcing the roof.
A $5 million hotel reconstruction was completed, leading local authorities to deem the building possibly the safest in the country.
The disaster was cited in arguments against the Reagan administration's attempt to eliminate an agency of the National Bureau of Standards.
The reconstructed hotel was officially renamed the Hyatt Regency Crown Center.
